aAbout: Argos Atlas is a hosted real-time world map that aggregates already-open official feeds — above all public cameras, which it claims number over 200,000 from official portals in more than 190 countries — and paints everything that moves around them on one flat map: flights, ships, war frontlines, verified events, infrastructure, earthquakes, fires and prediction markets. The live map is free with a free account; ARGOS PRO adds recording, history, an AI analyst layer and a 3D globe mode.
aStrengths: Argos Atlas is the broader live atlas around the story: the biggest claimed camera catalogue, live flights and ships with sanctions and dark-vessel flags, earthquakes, fires and infrastructure layers, prediction markets, and — for paying tiers — camera recording with a 24-hour archive, flight and ship history (7–90 days), geofence alerts and a 16-camera videowall. Where LiveUAMap stops at the reported event, Argos lets you look at the place itself and at everything moving around it, from any browser with a free account.
bAbout: LiveUAMap — the Live Universal Awareness Map — is an independent global news and information site founded in 2014 to cover the Ukrainian conflict and since expanded to more than 30 regions and topics. Its model is editorial: proprietary AI web crawlers surface newsworthy stories from open sources, and a group of expert analysts fact-checks them before dedicated editors plot them on per-region maps, backed by a complete chronological archive. It covers conflicts, human rights, protests, terrorism, weapons deployment, health, natural disasters and weather stories — as reported events, not as live sensor or camera layers.
bStrengths: LiveUAMap is the deeper newsroom: more than a decade of continuous operation since 2014, analyst fact-checking behind every plotted story, more than 30 region and topic maps, and a complete chronological archive for researching how an event unfolded. Its native iOS and Android apps, breaking-news notifications, and (on PRO) satellite maps, custom regions and data export make it a focused, trusted companion for following specific conflicts and crises day by day.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. Argos Atlas is a hosted live atlas built around camera scale (200,000+ claimed), live flights and ships, verified events and prediction markets — free to open with a free account, paid to record and remember. LiveUAMap is a human-verified news map founded in 2014: analyst-fact-checked stories across 30+ regions with a deep chronological archive, and no flights, ships, cameras or globe. If you want to *watch* a place live, open Argos Atlas; if you want to *follow* a conflict's verified story, open LiveUAMap.

faqs.q: Is LiveUAMap the same as Argos Atlas?

faqs.a: Argos Atlas, and it is not close: it claims 200,000+ public cameras in 190+ countries. LiveUAMap has no camera network — it maps reported stories, not live feeds. For comparison, WorldEye's directory lists 74,229 public cameras.
faqs.q: Which has live cameras, Argos Atlas or LiveUAMap?

faqs.a: LiveUAMap does not require an account to view its maps — the free web version is publicly accessible, with advertising. Argos Atlas is also free, but the map itself is used with a free account (Google or an email link).
faqs.q: Do I need an account for either?

faqs.a: Neither has a free one. LiveUAMap's free version is supported by advertising; its paid options are an ad-free account at $9.54 per half-year and PRO from $7/month. Argos Atlas's free map also shows ads; its ARGOS PRO plans remove them, starting at €15.99/month list (OUTPOST). No free trial is stated for either on the official pages checked.
faqs.q: Which is cheaper to use without ads?

faqs.a: Only Argos Atlas — and only on paid tiers. Its 3D globe starts at DISTRICT (€56.99/month list); the free tier is a flat map. LiveUAMap is a flat, 2D region-map product with no globe.

LiveUAMap. intro: Argos Atlas and LiveUAMap both put conflicts and world events on a map — one by watching, the other by reporting. Argos Atlas is a hosted website built around public cameras, which it claims number over 200,000 in more than 190 countries, layered with flights, ships, verified events, 16 frontlines and prediction markets, free with a free account. LiveUAMap, founded in 2014, is an independent news map covering more than 30 regions: AI crawlers find stories from open sources, human analysts fact-check them, and editors plot them — with no flights, no ships, no cameras and no globe.
pricingA: The live atlas is free and, in Argos's words, 'will stay free' — it asks for a free account and shows ads with camera limits. ARGOS PRO (EUR, VAT included in the EU/UK) lists OUTPOST at €15.99/month or €44.99 for 12 months, DISTRICT at €56.99/month or €134.99 for 12 months, DIVISION at €199/month or €809 for 12 months, and AGENCY at €1,049.99/month for registered companies. First-month welcome discounts apply to OUTPOST and DISTRICT; there is no free trial.
pricingB: The web map is free with advertising; the free version no longer shows joint regions or historic data for previous years. An ad-free account — 'removes advertising only' — costs $9.54 per half-year. PRO, from $7/month, removes advertising and adds satellite maps, location search, history, all regions and events, custom regions, notifications and data export. Enterprise and API services are offered, but no price is published on the official pages checked, and no free trial is stated.

verdictA: Choose Argos Atlas if you want to watch events, not just read them — live cameras, flights and ships around a verified-events map — and you are willing to pay for recording, the 3D globe and history.
verdictB: Choose LiveUAMap if you want a trusted, human-verified account of specific conflicts and crises — 30+ regions, a chronological archive back through a decade of reporting, and inexpensive PRO — mapped as news, not as live feeds.
verdictLine: Argos Atlas is the live atlas — it shows you the place, the traffic and the verified event together. LiveUAMap is the verified chronicle — it shows you the fact-checked story, region by region, and how it unfolded. Watch with Argos; follow with LiveUAMap.
worldEye: If Argos's account wall is the friction in one, and LiveUAMap's missing live layers are the gap in the other, WorldEye is the middle path: a hosted globe that opens free in any browser with no signup at all — 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries. It does not claim Argos's 200,000+ camera scale or its recording archive, and it does not offer LiveUAMap's analyst-fact-checked newsroom or its chronological archive. Its Pro tier ($7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year) sits between LiveUAMap PRO and ARGOS PRO on price.
